findings: The ordinary app immediately handles host.load rejection and closes its host on non-persisted pagehide. Actor-art ownership also keeps native work owned until retirement.
main(work) stores the returned native promise before its preparation admission promise settles. No rejection handler is installed on that result until the admission .then adopts it.
The actual createMediaPreparation scheduler normally resolves this admission in the same microtask checkpoint; ordinary rejection and synchronous throw tests produce zero unhandled events.

A controlled scheduler that delays admission after real native submission exposes a transient unhandled rejection before later handling. Cancellation still returns AbortError, but the unobserved native result also rejects transiently.

Normalizing exactly once with Promise.resolve(work()), observing result.catch immediately, and still returning that same result preserves primary rejection, cancellation, thenable execution count and late bitmap ownership.
